meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'этому').

examples.text: Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: That's why I'm running for a second term.
I'm tired, so I'm at home.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very, very much', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('necessary, needed').
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to run, to flee', paired with 'побежать'.

examples.trans: Run, Marina, before it's too late!
Where are you running so fast?

examples.text: Надо бежать! Беги в деревню к маме.
examples.trans: You need to run! Run to the village to your mum's.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for; behind', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Common feminine noun meaning 'friendship' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Конечно, между нами только крепкая искренняя дружба.
examples.trans: Of course, between us there is only strong sincere friendship.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'помнить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to remember, to recall', paired with 'вспоминать'.

examples.text: Я этого не хочу. Но вспомни, у тебя сын болеет.
examples.trans: I don't want that. But remember, your son is ill.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: He says nasty things about me.

examples.text: Как интересно! А в Москве ты про меня гадости рассказываешь.
examples.trans: How interesting! And in Moscow you go around saying nasty things about me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овесть'). Common feminine noun meaning 'conscience' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Нина, имей совесть! Я вчера ради вас всё сделал.
examples.trans: Nina, have a heart! Yesterday I did everything for you.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'изойти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to happen', paired with 'происходить'.

examples.text: Я не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: I don't know how it happened.

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, простите меня, пожалуйста. Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, please forgive me. I don't know myself how it happened.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to drink', paired with 'выпить'.

related.gloss: to go on a drinking binge

examples.text: Всё, теперь ты герой? И можно только пить?
examples.trans: So now you're a hero? And all you have to do is drink?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'over, above; at', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The lamp is above the table.

examples.text: За поведение? Вы смеётесь надо мной?
examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'less, fewer, smaller', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! А ты заикаешься меньше.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! And you stutter less.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'in short; shorter', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Короче, Самсон, сегодня ты приводишь её к Димону.
examples.trans: In short, Samson, tonight you bring her to Dimon's place.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'сказать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'tell', paired with 'рассказывать'.

examples.text: Он же слабый, сразу всё расскажет!
examples.trans: He's weak, after all—he'll tell us everything straight away!

examples.text: Я сегодня же расскажу всё Самсону!
examples.trans: I'll tell Samson everything this very day!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'again', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучайность'). Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'accident, chance' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Поверь, это была просто глупая случайность!
examples.trans: Believe me, it was just a stupid accident!

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must, should; owe').

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'truth; honestly' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'socks' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты обещал мне носки не разбрасывать.
examples.trans: You promised me not to scatter your socks.

examples.text: Носки я уже совсем не разбрасываю.
examples.trans: I do not scatter my socks anymore at all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'more; still; yet', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my own', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

examples.text: А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: And let them build their shopping centres.
